writeup: TIC 355734894 is a candidate eclipsing binary star with an orbital period of 9.26 days, detected through automated analysis of TESS photometry. The primary eclipse produces a dimming of 0.10%, with a detection signal-to-noise ratio of 14.0 in the BLS periodogram. Pixel-level difference imaging confirms the signal at the target location with a peak signal-to-noise of 8.4, though the centroid offset of 11.6 arcsec raises a question about whether the source lies slightly outside the formal target aperture. No secondary eclipse was detected. The candidate does not appear in six major variable-star catalogs. One important caveat: alternating eclipses show significantly different depths, suggesting the true period may be twice the initially measured value, which is why the corrected period of 9.26 days is reported here.
